title: Erdős #871: Partitioning Additive Bases of Order 2

problemStatement.plain: Formalize the additive-bases counterexample target: an order-2 additive basis A with representation counts r_A(n) tending to infinity that still cannot be partitioned into two disjoint order-2 additive bases.
whyMatters: Larsen's recent disproof settles a concrete Erdős additive-bases partition question.
The remaining axioms are named published construction results, making the next formalization targets explicit.
The blocking construction may be decomposable into reusable additive-combinatorics and representation-function lemmas.

proven: Larsen (2026) disproves the original Erdős partition question using an extension of the Erdős-Nathanson (1989) blocking construction.
Erdős-Nathanson (1989) proves a positive partition result under sufficiently strong logarithmic representation growth.
open: Reduce or formalize the Lean axioms currently standing for the Erdős-Nathanson and Larsen construction results, especially larsen_construction_blocking.
knownResults.goal: Survey and formalize additive-combinatorics ingredients needed to reduce the current 3-axiom Lean development.

currentState.focus: Axiom reduction for the additive-bases partition counterexample, starting with the Larsen 2026 blocking construction.
currentState.nextAction: Read Erdos871Problem.lean in full, then survey Mathlib additive-combinatorics, set-cardinality, density, and sumset APIs for blocking-property infrastructure.

knowledge.progressSummary: OBSERVE-phase Lean target: the gallery file has 3 remaining axioms for published additive-bases results, and the current work is to reduce those axioms rather than treat the target as fully formalized.
insights: The target asks for an order-2 additive basis A with r_A(n) -> infinity that cannot be partitioned into two order-2 additive bases.
Local notes identify three active axioms: erdos_nathanson_1989, erdos_nathanson_positive, and larsen_construction_blocking.
The primary reduction target is larsen_construction_blocking because the Larsen 2026 construction is described as constructive and block-based.
Mathlib survey targets include Combinatorics.Additive, Set/Card infrastructure, density lemmas, and sumset APIs.
nextSteps: Survey Mathlib.Combinatorics.Additive and related Salem/Behrend files for reusable sumset or density infrastructure.
Map the explicit Larsen blocking construction into smaller formal lemmas before attempting to discharge larsen_construction_blocking.
